cohort: The study included 188 term pregnant women (39-41 weeks gestation) with no pre-existing comorbidities.
finding: Increased fetal adiposity showed a significant positive correlation with maternal pre-pregnancy BMI and neonatal birth weight, and was strongly associated with higher rates of adverse perinatal outcomes including emergency cesarean delivery, atonic postpartum hemorrhage, low-APGAR scores, and respiratory distress.
mod_finding: Women in the higher fetal adiposity group demonstrated significantly higher rates of emergency cesarean delivery.
